**Astur v2.8.3** — the bar shows each window's own icon, keeps up when an app
changes it, and one hung program no longer takes the window manager with it.

## Download

`astur-windows-x64.zip` holds `astur.exe` and `astur_settings.py`.

## What changed

- **Icons come from the window, not the exe file.** The bar and the launcher
  now ask the window for its icon (`WM_GETICON`, then its class icon) and fall
  back to the exe only when the window has none, which is how the Windows
  taskbar does it. Every Python script shows the icon it set, instead of all of
  them showing the same interpreter icon.
- **The bar follows an icon that changes.** A window that swaps its own icon
  while it runs (a chat badge count, a document's modified mark) sends no
  event; the icon worker now re-reads the windows the bar shows every couple of
  seconds and re-resolves the ones that changed, in place, without a restart.
- **A hung app can no longer stall the window manager.** `ShowWindow`,
  `BringWindowToTop`, `SetWindowPos` and `SetWindowPlacement` all wait until the
  target app answers — measured to never return on a window that stopped
  pumping — and they ran on the thread that carries every hotkey, so one frozen
  program froze Astur. Shows, hides, raises and placements are now posted
  instead, and the calls with no posted form are skipped for a hung window.

## Notes

- **A hung window that already has the keyboard focus still keeps it**: Windows
  delivers those keys to the frozen program (and beeps), so hotkeys do not
  reach Astur until the focus moves elsewhere — click another window or the
  bar. Astur itself stays responsive throughout, and clicking its bar commands
  still works.
- No config key was added or changed, no default changed, and existing config
  files are never rewritten.
